executive_summary:
Episode 398 (presumed; title omits "| Ep N") opens by satirizing yesterday's Candyland illegal-nanny mansion comments (two nannies per child, elite Jewish agency, "we only hoard illegals") then pivots to Jennica Pounds (data republican): hired as a Department of War special government employee around the Tyler Robinson preliminary-hearing week, she posted a long X thread attacking Candace and defending the official 30-06 / NCRI / Erika-dehumanization narrative without disclosing DoD employment; she has now resigned, and the host mocks "where were you on 9/10."

The core beat is a paid anti-Candace clipping economy. Tips and an Atlantic investigation by Ali Breland describe Monster Lab / Clippet (DBA) and Elephant Clipping, run from Latvia by Matt Servius over Discord, paying editors by impressions (e.g. $120k August TPUSA generic pool at $300/1M views; $75k one-week Andrew Wilson debate pivot with instructions that Candace may appear only if she looks bad). Campaign Google Drives for Erika Kirk clips were uploaded beginning September 15, 2025 (five days after Charlie's assassination) by Enclave and Key staff (Jules Katz, Benjamin Goodman, Jack O'Hara); Enclave CEO Blake Wynn (Steve Wynn's nephew) is framed as Erika's close friend who appears beside her at medal, gala, and DoD emotional-asset moments. Andrew Kolvet denies TPUSA works with a Latvian company; the host calls that the audacity of the gaslight. Wayback Machine captures of Monster Lab from September 12, 2025 forward show only "loading," which the host treats as a wipe hiding the go-live date (possibly first Erika campaign). Blake's Fargo Talks "rare bucket" praise of Erika is played; a Las Vegas / Howard Hughes / Adelson / Wynn / Kash Patel syndicate thread is restated. Andrew Tate's Hustlers University is credited (via an Edson interview clip) as the clipping-economy pioneer. Closing comments revisit the unnamed fire-captain CPR dog-that-is-not-barking, ask who sponsors the Latvian operator, push moretips@candace.com tip intake, mock shifting smear packages, advise starving paid clippers of impressions, note sponsor-threat campaigns, and plug Conspiracy Girly merch.

claims.label: Jennica Pounds posted anti-Candace DoD-week thread without disclosing hire
claims.claim: The host says Jennica Pounds (data republican), hired by the Department of War as a special government employee around the Tyler Robinson preliminary-hearing week in July, posted a long X thread attacking Candace and her audience's treatment of Erika, reinforcing the NCRI report and a 30-06 deer analogy, without disclosing she was working for DoD; the thread was boosted by Andrew Kolvet and Bill Aman as if organic.
claims.investigative_direction: Archive the thread + employment paperwork dates; compare boost graph to paid clipping windows.

claims.label: Jennica Pounds announces resignation from Department of War
claims.claim: The host reads Pounds's X resignation from the Department of War (honoring Hegseth leadership; stepping back for book tour and midterms) and calls her a fraud for not revealing the DoD role, adding a joking "where were you on 9/10" jab.
claims.investigative_direction: Preserve resignation post; confirm SGE appointment dates vs thread timestamps.

claims.label: Tips describe million-dollar Discord bounties for anti-Candace videos
claims.claim: The host says unsolicited email tips claimed participants had proof that roughly $1.5M (and "millions") went out via Discord assignments for anti-Candace videos during the Tyler Robinson prelim week, orchestrated through Monster Lab / Clippet rather than a direct TPUSA paycheck.
claims.investigative_direction: Preserve tip emails; match Discord campaign IDs and payout ledgers if obtainable.

claims.label: August TPUSA clipping campaign banned Candace and Dean Withers
claims.claim: On a leaked Monster Lab / Elephant Clipping campaign card, the host shows a $120,000 August 3-31 pool at $300 per 1M views for Charlie Kirk / TPUSA clips with explicit instructions: only approved Turning Point affiliates; Candace Owens, Dean Withers, and others are not approved figures.
claims.investigative_direction: Hash-preserve campaign screenshots and Discord message IDs.

claims.label: Discord pivoted $75k to make Andrew Wilson look good vs Candace
claims.claim: After the August 14 Candace vs Andrew Wilson debate, Elephant Clipping Discord instructions shifted for one week to a $75,000 pool clipping only that debate, allowing Candace only where she looks bad and Turning Point looks good, despite TPUSA publicly saying it had nothing to do with the debate.
claims.investigative_direction: Align Discord timestamps with TPUSA public denial statements.

claims.label: Atlantic: Latvian Elephant Clipping pays foreign clippers to astroturf GOP feeds
claims.claim: Per Ali Breland's Atlantic investigation as read on air, Matt Servius in Latvia runs Elephant Clipping / Clippet paying Eastern Europe and Global South subcontractors to post bite-sized conservative clips designed to look like organic American GOP support, with Discord as the staffing channel and budgets sometimes listed near $900,000; the piece also lists banned subjects including RFK Jr., Megyn Kelly, Nick Fuentes, Tucker Carlson, and Riley Gaines, plus paid sub-campaigns for Vivek Ramaswamy and Tulsi Gabbard and $30k Shapiro/Crowder campaigns.
claims.investigative_direction: Preserve Atlantic article + Servius promo videos; map budget months to Candace harassment windows.

claims.label: Host ties $900k Feb/Mar/Apr campaigns to Bride of Charlie launch and Italy smear wave
claims.claim: The host notes Atlantic-reported ~$900k February and March/April "famous US political commentator" campaigns coincide with her Erika Kirk Bride of Charlie series launch and a March/April Italy confirmation-week harassment wave (drunk-driving husband claims, Vatican Russian-summit claims, Trump calling her vile), suggesting those budgets targeted her.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify the unnamed commentator campaigns' target lists from Discord/Drive artifacts.

claims.label: Kolvet denies TPUSA works with Latvian clipping company
claims.claim: The host reads Andrew Kolvet telling the Atlantic he can "pretty much guarantee" TPUSA is not working with a Latvian company and that contractors are unfamiliar with the clipping firm; she rejects the denial as gaslight given Erika clip drives and million-dollar budgets in TPUSA's orbit.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare Kolvet statement to Discord TPUSA campaign language and Enclave drive metadata.

claims.label: Erika Kirk clips uploaded to campaign drives September 15 2025 via Enclave staff
claims.claim: Per the Atlantic account the host highlights, Google Drive folders for the TPUSA-linked campaign contained mostly Erika Kirk videos uploaded September 15, 2025 (five days after Charlie's assassination) by Enclave and Key employees Jules Katz, Benjamin Goodman, and Jack O'Hara, with Blake Wynn as Enclave CEO.
claims.investigative_direction: Subpoena/archive drive file lists and uploader emails; identify which widow clips were seeded.

claims.label: Enclave deleted campaign drives after Atlantic outreach
claims.claim: The host reads that after Breland contacted the Wynns and Enclave, campaign video folders uploaded by Katz and O'Hara disappeared, Goodman reposted files from a non-Enclave email, Elephant Clipping / US politics channels were delisted from public Clippet Discords, Monster Lab campaign descriptions were stripped, and Enclave drives were taken down.

claims.label: Wayback Machine shows only loading for Monster Lab captures from September 12 2025

claims.label: Host senses Erika Kirk was the first Monster Lab campaign
